title: inspect takes option_id but choose takes choice, so the obvious sequence fails
body:
Two tools that operate on the same story option name its identifier differently:

    inspect_overworld_session_story   takes  option_id
    choose_overworld_session_story    takes  choice

So the natural sequence — inspect an option, then choose the one you inspected — fails on
the first attempt. Passing `option_id` to choose is rejected with:

    Input validation error: Required at choice

Confirmed live in a reference-tier session: inspected `albany:road_warden`, passed the
same id to choose under the same argument name, and was refused. The second attempt with
`choice` succeeded with an otherwise identical call.

This was recorded as finding F4 in docs/REPO_AUDIT_2026-08.md as an ergonomic asymmetry;
this is the first observation of it actually costing a call in play. It belongs to the
same family as the action-discovery overhead already filed: the cost is not one round
trip in isolation but one per player who follows the obvious sequence, on a surface
designed for mass-parallel cheap models.

Cheapest fix: accept `option_id` on choose as an alias for `choice`, keeping `choice` as
canonical so no stored trace or existing caller changes meaning. A rejection that named
the expected argument would also have turned this from a lookup into a correction.

evidence.summary: Audit finding F4, now observed costing a real failed call in a reference-tier session.
